A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GaussianGPT with the same authors, core method, and research objectives. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across additions, relocations, and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original GaussianGPT generation scores on PhotoShape (Table 1), serialization experiments (Table 2), and qualitative scene-generation and completion results, including ScanNet++ results in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains original generation experiments and adds quantitative scene comparisons, component and autoencoder ablations, inference measurements, and spatial-degradation results.

M1.justification: The sparse LFQ autoencoder, interleaved position/feature tokens, separate prediction heads, 3D RoPE transformer, and sliding-window outpainting remain unchanged. Five-retry resampling already appears in v1 Appendix B; its expanded explanation and the new ablation variants do not establish a change to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use PhotoShape, 3D-FRONT, ASE, and ScanNet++ v2. Shape and scene generation, completion with quarter/half context, and 12 m × 12 m outpainting were already covered. The additions quantify retained scenarios and examine the existing autoencoder rather than introduce new datasets or task coverage.

E2.justification: The chair-generation comparator set remains π-GAN, EG3D, DiffRF, and L3DG. v2 adds L3DG with RePaint to the previously unopposed scene-completion evaluation and conventional vector quantization against LFQ in Table 7. These are focused comparator additions; retraining L3DG on matched chunks primarily changes its evaluation setting.

E3.justification: v2 adds controlled scene comparisons using matched chunk training, 256×256 renderings, 16k Gaussian-center points, layout and CLIP metrics, 1,000 generation samples, and 200 held-out contexts with five completions each. Serialization scoring changes from results after 40 epochs to averages over epochs 70–74. New protocols also cover 20-epoch autoencoder comparisons and A100 timing with resampling and backward repainting disabled.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained serialization ablation, v2 tests separate vocabularies and positional encodings (Table 4), autoencoder downsampling and quantization choices (Table 7), and spatial degradation with 0, 5, or 15 retries (Figure 9). It also reports a failed hard-occupancy constraint and analyzes runtime and memory versus available context. These substantially broaden the questions examined.

E5.justification: v1 gives approximate average generation times without dispersion or sample counts. v2 Appendix B and Table 5 report runtime means and standard deviations, plus mean peak memory, across 100 samples. This adds uncertainty reporting for inference measurements, without establishing repeated training runs or uncertainty estimates for generation-quality scores.

E6.justification: v2 adds scene, component-ablation, efficiency, reconstruction, and degradation results. Its new matched scene-generation comparison reports FID 94.85 versus L3DG's 100.98, but lower COV, 0.548 versus 0.692. Serialization train/validation CE changes from 2.346/2.444 to 2.151/2.421 under a different epoch window, so this is not a same-setting gain. The approximate GH200 chunk time changes from 90 to 80 seconds. Chair scores in Table 1 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The loss equations and autoregressive formulation are unchanged; Equation 1 is merely repositioned. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs, and the new empirical analyses do not introduce substantive mathematical reasoning or formal assumptions.

C1.justification: The abstract and two principal contributions retain their meaning. The conclusion expands its performance claim from improved shape quality and qualitative scene demonstrations to stronger scene-generation and completion perceptual/layout quality, explicitly qualified by a geometric-diversity trade-off.

C2.justification: v2 substantially qualifies the earlier account of coherent large-scene generation by explaining accumulated degradation, directional asymmetry, and the retry-quality trade-off. It adds interpretations of weaker unconditional geometric diversity, sequential sampling costs, cache-dominated memory, and reconstruction-versus-token-length trade-offs. Existing real-world limitations remain, while the new discussion establishes additional practical boundaries.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies 2k mesh-surface points for the retained chair evaluation, explains cache allocation and benchmarking controls, and corrects the printed AdamW epsilon from 1^(-10) to 10^(-10). Most architecture, training, optimizer, and backend-commit disclosures are retained. These documentation additions and corrections do not establish that the underlying retained experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: All 77 earlier references are retained. Six additions cover RePaint, Neural Discrete Representation Learning, Flash-Decoding, Medusa, and two speculative-decoding papers. They support the new comparisons and efficiency discussion; the main related-work narrative and positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 trims introductory prose, reorders dataset descriptions, integrates scene completion into Scene Synthesis, expands and renames the ablation section, and revises the conclusion and outpainting discussion. Appendix sections are added around the new analyses. Editing and restructuring are concentrated in these areas; the abstract, related work, and method exposition are largely retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds substantial displays: scene metrics, component ablations, efficiency, and autoencoder tables, plus a three-panel degradation heatmap and two chunked-L3DG galleries. The serialization table is reformatted beside the component ablation. Existing qualitative figures are retained, with relocations and revised captions; v1 Figures 9–11 become v2 Figures 12–14.

improvement.justification: v1 supports its central scene-generation capabilities mainly through qualitative examples. v2 substantially addresses that evidential gap with matched scene-generation and completion comparisons, while adding ablations that test important design choices. Runtime measurements and degradation analyses also make the computational, geometric-diversity, and long-horizon limitations explicit. Together, these additions substantially strengthen empirical support and the calibration of the paper's conclusions.
